scope: The Privacy & Security page (/trust): its release evidence, the How Blanc works rows, the connections list, and the Security and Private tabs guides it embeds, re-checked against public v1.52.0 on November 23, 2026. Earlier wording was last checked against v1.25.0 (app explanations) and v1.27.0 (release evidence).

releaseVerification.qualification: v1.52.0 was published on November 21, 2026 with both Mac architectures (DMG and zip), one Windows installer with windows-signature.json, one x86_64 AppImage, SHA256SUMS, its Sigstore bundle and a CycloneDX SBOM; Linux ships only the AppImage (package.json linux target). The release record, completed after the tag at 06783061, says under Independent verification that both DMGs passed Gatekeeper (notarized Developer ID), strict deep codesign, the pinned leaf, stapler validate, build 1520 and their architecture; windows-signature.json is Valid with the expected publisher and matches the installer's SHA-256; SHA256SUMS passed 16 of 16 and cosign verified the bundle; hosted smoke passed the published AppImage. The record distinguishes hosted checks (native run, hosted smoke), checks on the release Mac and owner approvals (three acceptance scenarios run on the MacBook Pro, the ecs-signing gate under the standing release approval); it records no waiver. docs/release-verification.md at the tag still gives the files, cosign and per-platform signature steps.

syncFindings.qualification: docs/security-assessment.md (identical at the tag and on main) still lists the account-locator authorization (R3) and the non-atomic write and delete races (R5) as open. The request-size cap (#474, MAX_REQUEST_BYTES) is in production blanc-sync since its November 2 deployment (cloudflare/sync-worker/README.md, test/unit/sync-worker-limits.test.js), so the sentence saying it was not deployed is retired. No independent external audit has been commissioned.

licensing.qualification: LICENSE, ASSET-LICENSE.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md exist at v1.52.0 and the page links them at that tag; the app explanations on the page were re-read against the tag's source for this record.

blocking.qualification: Blanc Blocker compiles only the bundled, hash-verified EasyList and EasyPrivacy snapshots (adblock/sources/pinned.json) and its loader has no fetch capability. Since v1.27 Settings → Privacy & Security offers uBlock Origin as the blocking provider for regular tabs; its Settings text says 'Filter lists update automatically', and private tabs keep Blanc Blocker (src/main/ublock-provider.js). The shield chip and popover show a blocked count and a per-site switch, not a list of what was blocked (copy/messages/en.json shield keys).

localNetwork.qualification: Since v1.50.0 (#1593) a website's request to this device or the local network raises a Blanc prompt for the top-level site, remembered per site and kept in memory only in private sessions; cross-origin frames are refused without a prompt (src/main/local-network-access.js, permissions.js PROMPTED and localNetworkPolicyFor). Media, location and notifications remain the other prompted permissions.

search.qualification: Bangs are on by default (settings.js bangsEnabled: true, since v1.36) and send a search to the bang's site instead of the selected engine; !w is in the bundled catalog. Suggestions go to the selected provider only, never from private tabs or for recognized sensitive input (src/main/search-suggestions.js).

bangIcons.qualification: bang-icons-policy.js asks https://blanc.day/bang-icons/<host> only for hosts in the built-in catalog, never for a host from your own bangs, and not while a private tab is active or before setup completes.

siteIcons.qualification: favicon-network.js fetches a site's icon itself, with no cookies, referrer or page and session state, to keep it for favorites, bang rows and shared tabs.

whatsNew.qualification: After a feature update whats-new-check.js sends one HEAD to blanc.day with credentials 'omit' and no referrer to learn whether that release's What's New page exists, and whats-new.js opens it once in a tab.

protectedMedia.qualification: Since v1.43.0 Blanc downloads Google's Widevine component through castLabs ECS's component updater and later checks there for updates (drm-runtime.js). The earlier 'without cookies' had no evidence in Blanc's code at the tag (the request belongs to the component updater), so it is dropped.

sync.qualification: Sync's encrypted stores at the tag are bookmarks, settings, session, icons, sends (pages sent to another device, v1.44) and spaces (src/main/sync.js STORES, src/main/sends.js). Since v1.45 Sync can be turned on without a passphrase, with a random key and a recovery code, and devices join with a pairing code (sync.js startNew, sync-pairing.js); a passphrase, when used, is never stored or sent, and the retained key is wrapped by the operating system credential service.

passkeys.qualification: Blanc's own Secure Enclave passkeys are Mac only (setupWebAuthn returns unless the platform is darwin); on Windows, passkeys go through Windows' own dialog.

onePassword.qualification: 1Password fill is available on macOS, Windows and Linux but isOnePasswordDeviceSupported refuses Windows on Arm, where the x64 app cannot load the Arm64 SDK library; fill is off by default.

privateSessions.qualification: Each profile has its own private session: Personal uses private-browsing and each named profile private-browsing-<id> (profile-sessions.js privatePartitionFor), discarded when Blanc quits.

websiteMeasurement.qualification: This describes the website, not the app. site.js turns Google measurement on by default outside consent-required regions and requires a saved opt-in in the EEA, UK and Switzerland (and when the location is unknown), as the privacy policy says; the footer's Privacy choices turn it off.

claims.exactWording: Blanc Blocker applies network rules and cosmetic filters from bundled, hash-verified EasyList and EasyPrivacy snapshots. It does not fetch changing filter lists or remote scriptlet resources at startup. Reviewed list updates arrive with a new Blanc release. If you choose uBlock Origin instead in Settings, it updates its filter lists from their publishers; private tabs keep Blanc Blocker.

claims.exactWording: Browsing sends requests to those sites and their resources. Blocking reduces known ads and trackers; it cannot stop every form of tracking. Since Blanc 1.50, a website asks before it reaches this device or your local network.

claims.exactWording: Blanc 1.43.0 and later download Google’s Widevine component so sites can play protected video and music. Blanc asks Google’s component update service for it, and later checks there for updates. A site’s player sends its license requests to the license server that site chooses.

claims.exactWording: A submitted search goes to your selected search engine, or to the site a bang names (such as !w). If suggestions are enabled, eligible typed prefixes also go to that provider. claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: If you enable Sync, eligible Favorites, settings, optional open-tab snapshots, pages you send to another device and, since Blanc 1.45, Spaces you choose to share are encrypted before reaching Blanc’s Cloudflare-hosted service. Cookies, passwords and browsing history are not synced.

claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: This website has separate choices. Cloudflare counts page views without cookies, and the download redirect counts aggregate downloads. Google analytics and limited ad-conversion measurement require opt-in in the EEA, UK and Switzerland and are on by default elsewhere; you can turn them off through the footer’s Privacy choices. Turning them off prevents future optional measurement.
claims.subject: Blanc website

claims.exactWording: Blanc Blocker runs inside the browser, not as an extension. Reviewed EasyList and EasyPrivacy snapshots are hash-pinned into each Blanc release; the browser does not fetch changing filter scriptlets at startup. The shield shows how much was blocked on each page. How blocking works.
claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: On a Mac with Touch ID, Blanc creates device-bound passkeys inside Apple’s Secure Enclave. The private key never leaves the chip, and Blanc is signed with an Apple-issued Developer ID and provisioned to hold its own keychain access group. Secure Enclave passkeys are macOS only for now.
claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: Camera, microphone, location, notifications, the local network — each request raises a Blanc prompt, and each decision is remembered for that site. Decisions made in a private tab are never written to disk.
claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: Optional 1Password fill on macOS, Windows and Linux (not Windows on Arm).
claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: Sync is off by default. Favorites, eligible settings, optional open-tab snapshots and, since Blanc 1.45, Spaces you choose to share are encrypted on your device. The current v1 server stores ciphertext under an opaque account locator and cannot read or merge it. A passphrase, if you use one, is never stored or sent, and the retained key is wrapped by the operating system credential service.
claims.subject: Blanc

claims.exactWording: Private tabs share one separate in-memory browsing session with other private tabs of the same profile opened during the same Blanc run; they do not share cookies or site storage with regular tabs, and the private session is discarded when Blanc quits. Websites, downloads, your network, or an employer may still observe activity, and files you explicitly save remain on disk.
claims.subject: Blanc
